title: Welding and cutting
summary: Which stick rod to use, typical amps by rod diameter, and the lens shade needed for each process. Also covers galvanised and coated metal fumes, angle grinder safety, and the basics and never-do list for oxy-fuel cylinders.

steps.text: Before striking an arc, put on a helmet with the right lens shade, cover your skin, and screen bystanders.
steps.warn: Looking at the arc without a proper lens causes arc eye, which is painful and often not felt until hours later.

steps.text: Pick a rod for the job and set the amps from the diameter table. Keep 7018 dry.

Check the metal. Strip galvanised, painted or plated metal and ventilate. Never weld or cut a container that held fuel: see [Hot work on drums, tanks and cylinders](#guides/safety_hot_work_containers).
steps.warn: Zinc and coating fumes make you ill, and a respirator does not replace ventilation.

steps.text: For grinders and oxy-fuel, use the checklists: guard on, disc rated above grinder speed, cylinders upright and chained, no oil on oxygen fittings.

notes:
**Welding and cutting can blind, burn, poison and kill. For structural, pressure or vehicle safety parts (frames, brakes, steering, tanks), use a qualified welder if one can be reached.**

- Clear combustibles first (CCOHS welding hot work). Keep a fire watch after work stops: CCOHS advises at least 60 minutes, and up to 3 hours or more where the area needs it (CCOHS welding hot work); the US OSHA rule is at least 30 minutes (OSHA 1910.252). Plan on the longer time.
- The electrode and work are live. Wear dry, hole-free gloves, stand on dry insulation, and never dip a rod in water. (Lincoln guide)

## Never weld without eye protection
- The arc gives off invisible ultraviolet light. Looking at it unprotected causes arc eye: red, watering, gritty, painful eyes with light sensitivity, usually hours later. It generally clears in about a day, but see a doctor. (TWI)
- Use a helmet and lens that meet ANSI Z87.1. Cover skin, and screen bystanders: they must not watch the arc. (Lincoln guide) Fire watchers and helpers need lenses too. (OSHA fact sheet)
- Start with a shade too dark to see the weld, then step lighter, never below the minimum. (OSHA 1910.133)

| Process | Current or plate | OSHA minimum shade | ANSI/AWS suggested |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stick, under 3/32 in (2.4 mm) | under 60 A | 7 | - |
| Stick, 3/32 to 5/32 in | 60 to 160 A | 8 | 10 |
| Stick, over 5/32 to 1/4 in | over 160 to 250 A | 10 | 12 |
| Stick, over 1/4 in | over 250 to 550 A | 11 | 14 |
| MIG / flux-cored | 60 to 250 A | 10 | 11 to 12 |
| TIG | under 150 A | 8 | 10 to 12 |
| Gas welding | under 3.2 mm | 4 | 5 |
| Gas welding | 3.2 to 12.7 mm | 5 | 6 |
| Gas welding | over 12.7 mm | 6 | 8 |
| Oxygen cutting | under 25 mm | 3 | 4 |
| Oxygen cutting | 25 to 150 mm | 4 | 5 |

(OSHA fact sheet; OSHA 1910.133). These are US values; Canadian CSA tables were not checked.

## Stick rods

| Rod | Current | Good for | Watch for |
|---|---|---|---|
| E6010 | DC only | Deep penetration through rust, oil, paint, dirt. All positions. | Tight arc, harder to learn. |
| E6011 | AC or DC | Same deep arc on corroded, dirty metal. Use on AC-only welders. | Not low hydrogen. |
| E6013 | AC or DC | Soft arc, little spatter, easy slag. Clean, thin steel. | Moderate penetration only. |
| E7018 | AC or DC | Strong, tough welds, even in cold. Use where cracking is a risk (low alloy, high carbon, high sulfur steel) or thick plate. | Must be kept dry. Short arc, never whip. |

(Miller; Lincoln guide). 6010, 6011 and 6013 are not low hydrogen: avoid them on higher-strength or high-carbon steel. Run 6010 electrode positive. (Lincoln guide)

**Typical amperage (A), Lincoln rods**

| Rod and current | 3/32 in (2.4 mm) | 1/8 in (3.2 mm) | 5/32 in (4.0 mm) | 3/16 in (4.8 mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E6010 DC+ | 40-70 | 75-130 | 90-175 | 140-225 |
| E6011 AC | 50-85 | 75-120 | 90-160 | 120-200 |
| E6011 DC | 40-75 | 70-110 | 80-145 | 110-180 |
| E6013 AC | 75-105 | 110-150 | 160-200 | 205-260 |
| E6013 DC | 70-95 | 100-135 | 145-180 | 190-235 |
| E7018 DC+ | 70-110 | 85-150 | 125-200 | 170-260 |
| E7018-1 AC | 80-120 | 95-160 | 130-210 | 180-280 |

(Lincoln guide: Fleetweld 5P, 35 and 37; Excalibur 7018 and 7018-1). Use the lower part for vertical-up and overhead. Other brands differ.

**Rod storage:** keep opened 7018 at 120 to 150 °C (250 to 300 °F). Redry damp 7018 for 1 hour at 340 to 400 °C (650 to 750 °F), after a 1 to 2 hour pre-dry at 80 to 105 °C if it got wet. Do not go hotter. Other rods, if damp, go in a 40 to 50 °C (100 to 120 °F) cabinet only. (Lincoln storage)

## Fumes
- Zinc from galvanised steel makes zinc oxide fume (metal fume fever). Lead primers, cadmium plating, chromates, paints and plastic coatings also give toxic fumes. (CCOHS fumes)
- Remove coatings from the weld area first. Do not grind coatings: the dust may be toxic. (CCOHS fumes)
- Keep your head out of the fume. Use local exhaust near the arc; a respirator does not replace ventilation. Outdoors, stay upwind. (CCOHS fumes)
- Never weld near chlorinated solvent or degreaser vapour: it can form phosgene. (Lincoln guide)

## Angle grinder
- Keep the guard on. It should cover half the disc, between disc and you. (SafeWork SA)
- The disc's maximum rpm must be higher than the grinder's speed. Use the right flange and nut and a disc that fits the spindle. (SafeWork NSW; Cornell)
- Grinding discs grind; cutting discs cut. Never swap. Discard dropped or damaged discs. (SafeWork SA)
- Kickback: use light pressure; hold a grinding disc at 15 to 30° (a cutting disc goes in straight, never sideways); never bump the disc on the work, clamp the work, let it reach full speed first, and use both hands. Keep cut depth to no more than twice the disc thickness. (SafeWork SA; Cornell)
- Wear goggles or glasses plus a face shield, hearing protection and gloves. Unplug to change discs. (SafeWork SA; Cornell)

## Oxy-fuel (oxygen and acetylene)
- The flame is about 3,500 °C (6,330 °F) and cuts steel. A 2,000 psi oxygen cylinder can become a lethal projectile if it falls and the valve breaks. Keep cylinders upright and chained, caps on when not in use. (CDC torch guide; OSHA 1910.253)
- Fit flashback arrestors between torch and supply. Leak-test with soapy water after connecting; shut off gas if it leaks. (CSNS hot work; CDC torch guide)
- Acetylene must not be used above 15 psig (103 kPa). Open its valve no more than 1-1/2 turns. (OSHA 1910.253)
- Close cylinder valves when work stops. One guide's order: light fuel first, then add oxygen; at shutdown close oxygen then acetylene at the torch, close both cylinder valves, then bleed the lines. Follow your torch maker's order if it differs. (OSHA 1910.253; CDC torch guide)

**Never:**
- Never put oil or grease on oxygen cylinders, regulators, hoses or torches. (OSHA 1910.253)
- Never lift a cylinder by its cap, or move it with a magnet. (OSHA 1910.253; CSNS hot work)
- Never use oxygen to blow dust off clothes: they ignite easily. (CDC torch guide)
- Never store oxygen within 6 m (20 ft) of fuel gas, unless a 1.5 m (5 ft) noncombustible barrier with a half-hour fire rating is between. (OSHA 1910.253)
- Never cut or weld a container that held fuel, or may have, without a written procedure and gas testing. (CSNS hot work) See [Hot work on drums, tanks and cylinders](#guides/safety_hot_work_containers).

## When no help is coming

**Arc eye** (red, watering, gritty, painful eyes; light hurts)
- It is usually felt 6 to 12 hours after the flash, not at once (NHS Wales, TWI). Swollen lids and headache can come with it (NHS Wales).
- Remove contact lenses. Go somewhere dark. Rest with the eyes closed (AAO, NHS Wales). A cold washcloth over closed eyes helps (AAO). A clean, non-stick pad over the eyes is first aid for welder's flash (St John).
- Do not rub the eyes (AAO).
- Simple pain relief used as the label says is acceptable (NHS Wales).
- Expect it to settle on its own. Symptoms usually fade in a day or two (AAO). The surface heals in 24 to 48 hours, and vision usually returns after about 18 hours (NHS Wales).
- If there is no improvement in 24 hours, get it checked (NHS GG&C). Blurred, partly lost or double vision, or sharp pain, are danger signs (St John). A foreign body may be in the eye as well (TWI).
